instructions: Trim any big pieces of fat off the chicken thighs, then cut each thigh into 3 or 4 chunks. Pat them dry with paper towels and sprinkle the 1 1/2 tsp salt all over them.
Cut the sausage into 1 inch pieces. Seed the bell peppers and slice them into strips about 1/2 inch wide. Thinly slice the 6 garlic cloves.

Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Add half the chicken and half the sausage in a single layer with room between the pieces. Leave them alone for about 3 minutes, until the undersides are deep golden and let go of the pan.
Turn the pieces and brown the other sides for about 3 minutes. Transfer them to a plate. Brown the rest of the chicken and sausage the same way and add them to the plate.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the last 1 tbsp olive oil and the bell peppers and cook them for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft and starting to char at the edges.
Add the garlic and stir for about 1 minute, until it smells toasty but hasn't browned.

Return the chicken and sausage to the pan with any juices from the plate. Stand back a little and pour in the 1/3 cup vinegar. Let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until it's thick and syrupy.
Sprinkle the 1/2 tsp oregano over everything and turn the heat to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the chicken is tender and coated in a glossy sauce.
While it cooks, chop 2 tbsp of the parsley and slice 4 of the hot cherry peppers into a small bowl. Slice the bread.

Uncover the pan. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick piece there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink left.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a splash of the vinegar.
Scatter the parsley over the top. Serve with the bread, and the cherry peppers on the side.
method_notes: None of the versions read had 20 or more ratings (A Family Feast shows 8 reviews but no rating count, and RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for Italian, has no scarpariello), so this leads with Lidia Bastianich's version. Every version browns chicken and Italian sausage hard and builds a tangy pan sauce; Lidia's uses boneless thighs, garlic, white wine vinegar boiled to a syrup and dried oregano, then covers and cooks it low, while Pamela Salzman, Tasting Table and A Family Feast add bell peppers, onion, wine and stock and finish bone-in chicken in the oven. This follows Lidia's method and ratios, adds the sweet bell peppers the others use, and puts the hot cherry peppers on the side to keep the pan mild.
